13 July 2005

## Circular to Licensed Corporations and Registered Institutions

## Settlement of Disciplinary Cases

Recently, the SFC has received a number of enquiries about settlement of disciplinary cases. It  appears  that  some  regulated  persons  are  uncertain  about  the  SFC's  willingness  to  settle cases.

The law allows the SFC to settle disciplinary proceedings by agreement only when it is in the interest of the investing public or in the public interest to do so. Whether or not the SFC will settle a case depends on the facts and circumstances of individual cases. A regulated person who is subject to the SFC's disciplinary proceedings can always approach the SFC to see if it is possible to settle the proceedings by agreement. When the SFC receives realistic settlement proposals from a regulated person, the SFC may be willing to enter into negotiations with the person, although there is no guarantee that such negotiations will result in a settlement. The SFC is not obliged to settle a case if a regulated person asks it to.

The  SFC  has  briefly  explained  its  settlement  policy  in  a  pamphlet  entitled Disciplinary Proceedings at a Glance published in September 2004. Copies of the pamphlet are available at  the  SFC's  office  and  on  the  SFC's  website.  Moreover,  any  person  who  is  subject  to disciplinary proceedings would receive a copy of the pamphlet together with the document initiating the proceedings.

The pamphlet also summaries the SFC's disciplinary process including:

- the  factors  which  the  SFC  may  take  into  account  in  deciding  whether  to  start disciplinary proceedings and the level of sanctions;
- the disciplinary measures available to the SFC;
- the rights of appeal to the Securities and Futures Appeals Tribunal and the Court of Appeal.
- the rights of the subject of disciplinary proceedings in the process; and

Regulated  persons  or  anyone  who  are  interested  in  the  SFC's  disciplinary  process  and settlement policy can obtain a copy of the pamphlet from the SFC's office or visit the SFC's website at www.sfc.hk.

Enforcement Division Securities and Futures Commission
